title: Rising talent Arthur Fils adds Goran Ivanišević, Novak Djokovic’s former coach, on initial trial
content:
Rising men’s tennis star Arthur Fils is working with Goran Ivanišević, Novak Djokovic’s former coach, on a trial basis with a view to a longer-term partnership.

Ivanišević, the 2001 Wimbledon champion with whom Djokovic won 12 of his 24 Grand Slam titles, has been in Fils’ coaching box at the Qatar Open in Doha, alongside Ivan Cinkuš.

A source briefed on Ivanišević’s and Fils’ plans said the partnership is a trial, with positive feedback on both sides thus far. They will decide whether to extend the partnership after this week. The source described Ivanišević’s role as additional to that of fellow Croatian Cinkuš, who is friendly with Ivanišević and has been Fils’ coach since early 2025.

After beating compatriot Quentin Halys Wednesday, Fils said that Ivanišević is “a hell of a champion” during an interview with Tennis TV.

“I think it’s good for me, maybe it’s best for me, to have his experience as a coach, and a player. So I’m very glad that he’s going to join us, during this long journey,” he said.

Ivanišević, 54, who split with Djokovic in May 2024, most recently had ill-fated stints coaching first two-time Grand Slam champion Elena Rybakina, and then two-time Grand Slam finalist Stefanos Tsitsipas.

Ivanišević started working with Rybakina in November 2024, but split with her just two months later after she reinstated Stefano Vukov, who at the time was suspended by the WTA Tour during a Code of Conduct investigation, onto her team. Two people briefed on the WTA’s investigation, who had attended some of Rybakina’s recent events before the 2025 Australian Open, described Ivanišević as blindsided by Rybakina’s public announcement of Vukov’s return.

Ivanišević remained on Rybakina’s team until she went out of that Australian Open, at which point he confirmed his departure on social media. A spokesperson for Rybakina did not comment.

Ivanišević then started working with Tsitsipas in May 2025, but they split after another stint of two months during which Ivanišević criticized his new charge’s fitness. Tsitsipas described working with Ivanišević as “short but intense” in a statement. Ivanišević said that “nothing bad” led to their split.

Fils, 21, is attempting to rebuild after a back injury at the French Open ended a very promising 2025 season early. He reached world No. 14 before the injury, which he said in Paris related to an issue he has had since childhood, kept him out for seven months, despite a brief comeback attempt at last year’s Canadian Open.

He faces Czechia’s Jiří Lehečka in the quarterfinals at the Qatar Open Thursday.
